description.value:
Compatibility: Avian

Spelled “Yaġruda” in Ave, yarhuda are lightweight, bipedal avians with crooked beaks, piercing eyes, and long, wing-like ears. A plume of large, soft, water-retardant feathers covers most of their upper body, draping partially over their shoulders and midsection like a natural poncho or cloak. Their torso is covered with much smaller feathers, but their legs are mostly bereft, causing some yarhuda to wear armor and clothing beneath their plumes for safety and comfort. These plumed feathers serve more than just to shield them from the elements.

The yarhuda’s most striking ability, however, is their unusual, helicopter-like method of flight. The thickest and largest feathers around their neck are attached directly to a special cylindrical bone. Yarhuda can flex an internal muscle to make spin on its axis around its collarbone at high speeds, creating lift and allowing them to fly. Yarhuda have surprising control over all of their feathers, but especially these ‘propellers.’ They are able to angle or flare them at will to control their flight path. Yarhuda feathers can be quite rigid or sharp depending on the part of the body, and can be angled or flared out for use in controlling their trajectory or momentum. A yarhuda’s control over their feathers remains impeccable, able to open, flatten, or curve their rotor feathers even during flight. Furthermore, their heads are topped with a small pair of wings sprouting from their head like ears. These can be rapidly flapped to control which way they’re facing mid-flight and keep themselves from spiraling—a pair of natural second rotors. When combined with a lesser control over their arm and body feathers, yarhuda are able to move through the air with incredible ease.

Yarhuda usually have greyish skin with shades of blue or black, but their feathers have much more diversity. While typically falling into darker shades of blue, purple, or black, it’s possible for yarhuda to have dark greens, cyans, oranges, or browns. Very rarely, yarhuda are born with a mutation that gives their feathers especially vibrant colors, like that of a parrot. Regardless of color, their feathers have a slight iridescent sheen to it, and usually flow together naturally, rather than having sharp patterns. Yarhuda beaks are intense, often crooked or curved, and typically with calm grey, tan, or black colorations. However, it’s not uncommon for a yarhuda to wear beak paint as a show of style or affiliation. Dying feathers, especially bleaching them, is common for similar reasons.

In a similar way, a common aspect of yarhuda culture are masks, either over the head, beak, or both. While yahruda have neck feathers that block much air pushing up past their face, and have third clear eyelids (nictating membranes) common in many traditional avians to protect their eyes, many yahruda consider goggles and masks to be the safer, more comfortable, and more modular alternative. These evolved into gradually more elaborate masks, and have grown a unique cultural significance in most yahruda communities. Beyond this, leg wraps and pants are common amongst yarhuda to keep warm, with special light body armor that layers under their major plumage used when combat is involved. This gives yahruda a distinct “armorless” look in combat as their armor is often hidden from view.

Yarhuda can be found all over, but are particularly prevalent in high altitude, high-perching environments. They tend to build homes in precarious locations, such as atop of trees or on cliffs, as they have little fear of falling in these situations and give them easy lift for takeoff. This preference has forced yarhuda engineering to be particularly adept at supporting such precarious architecture.

Yarhuda are sometimes seen as wintry, with stoic faces and a strong exterior that often belie their more passionate nature. The wind is a gift, one that yarhuda never underestimate. Those who cannot fly may spend their time constructing wind-utilizing art or architecture. Some use their masterful feather control to make wind sculptures, transient and complex shapes made of air filled with fine-colored powder.

system.classDetails:
Core Yarhuda Traits

  • Attribute Increase: Your Dexterity increases by 1.
  • Lifespan: Yarhuda reach maturity around 8 and tend to live up to age 60.
  • Size: Medium; Yarhuda are tall avians with long legs and many feathers on their upper half. They tend to stand within a range of 5-6 feet tall, sometimes taller. Despite their broad appearance, they typically weigh 90-120lbs. Some branches range up to 200lbs.
  • Speed: Your base ground speed is 25 feet.
  • Languages: You can speak, read, and write Common and Ave.
  • Helix Wings: @Compendium[undertaking.abilities.H95D3RXCURCCV9WB]{Helix Wings}
  • High Altitude Adaption: @Compendium[undertaking.abilities.2OKY1SZ7O07S1SLX]{High Altitude Adaptation}
  • Racial Trinket: You own a pair of goggles or a yarhuda flight mask.
    Yarhuda masks and goggles are a common part of yarhuda culture, helping keep wind and dust out of their face during flight. These can vary in shape and design from simple leather googles, to long-nosed incense masks, to more flat-face masks.
